## Recent retrospectives

### 2026-08-31 — Design docs — scope decisions settled; chat, credits, materials, and retrieval designed

- **Went well:** Four design docs landed with stable, cross-referenced requirement IDs, so agents.md and e2e-walkthrough.md cite requirements.md rather than restating it, and markdownlint was run after every pass instead of at the end. Grounding the walkthrough in the two worked examples already in temp-references kept it concrete — the beats name real artifacts from the Tim Diercks study pack rather than inventing a demo. Pushing back on the direct-from-browser Supabase reading was right: it contradicts a shipped ADR and two implemented packages, and encoding it silently would have been worse than raising it. The claude-api skill's grep gate was run before writing about embeddings, which correctly routed to skipping it, and model IDs were kept out of retrieval.md so the doc cannot go stale on a version bump.
- **Improve:** The region-binding recommendation was wrong, and wrong in an avoidable way. Three options were offered — marquee, text-only, model-resolves — and model-resolves was steered away from because a silent mis-resolution produces a confident false measurement. But propose-and-confirm was already the established pattern in the very document being written, used twice for landmarks and perspective; synthesising it was the obvious fourth option and it was not offered. Laurie proposed it unprompted and it is strictly better. Separately, question 3 in that same AskUserQuestion was compressed to the point of being unclear — 'I don't understand what your question 3 is' — and the plain-language explanation given afterwards should have been the question. Two mechanical errors: the walkthrough beats were written in an order that put the plan after the chat that amends it and had to be reordered, and renumbering the FR-1000 block cascaded stale cross-references through three files that needed a mapped sweep to repair.
- **Tooling:** Stable requirement IDs across a doc set need a check. Renumbering one block silently broke cross-references in three files, and the only reason it was caught is that the numbers were re-grepped by hand. A trivial script that extracts every FR-NNN/NFR-NN definition from requirements.md and fails on a reference elsewhere in docs/design/ with no definition would have caught it instantly, and would keep catching it as the remaining five docs are written.
- **Decisions:**
  - Showcase vision tools are BOTH head construction and perspective (proposal option B); a cut order is written into requirements.md §9 because two high-uncertainty tools now sit on the critical path
  - Week 9 fine-tuning is omitted; learning_mapping.md must name it as a gap rather than let hybrid retrieval imply coverage
  - Voice is out of scope entirely, not sequenced behind HITL
  - Agent runtime is LangGraph behind FastAPI in python/services/agent; browser → Next.js route handler → Cloud Run, never browser → Python
  - Supabase Auth stays server-side per ADR 0002 — direct-from-browser auth was raised and flagged as an ADR amendment rather than encoded
  - Studio chat is in scope as a second entry point into the same graph, not a sixth agent
  - Chat effect on the plan is propose-and-accept; an accepted amendment re-runs the Plan Critic
  - Chat is metered in per-artist daily credits, weighted by route, on a ledger fully separate from the plan budget — exhausted credits never block plan creation (FR-1017)
  - Materials guidance is brand-neutral: specifications, never products, prices, or retailer links
  - Every plan carries a materials list (FR-607), which puts the materials corpus on the plan critical path; list-versus-stage agreement is a new materials_mismatch critic defect
  - Region binding is propose-and-confirm, not a marquee: the agent outlines where it believes the artist means, and only confirmed or adjusted regions back a measured claim
  - The same propose → confirm → recompute pattern now covers landmarks, perspective, and chat regions — one HITL mechanism on three surfaces, stated as a design principle
  - retrieval.md was added as a ninth design doc; the proposal had folded retrieval into architecture.md, which understated the largest technical claim in the capstone
  - Postgres FTS ranks with ts_rank_cd, which is not BM25 — start there, measure, and do not call it BM25 in the submission
  - The corpus is public-read to any authenticated principal and is not artist data; ownership RLS belongs on projects and transcripts, never on corpus tables
  - No cross-encoder reranker: the fine-tune was its reason to exist, so RRF's fused order is final
  - flows.json restructure is proposed in requirements.md §7 but not applied — the names are Laurie's and the file is a CI gate

### 2026-08-30 — Art Loupe scope proposal — reference-to-plan, artwork critique cut

- **Went well:** The reference corpus was binary — .docx and .xlsx — and was read directly by unzipping and stripping the XML rather than asking for conversions, so nothing in the brief went unread. The Explore agent's repo inventory changed the proposal materially rather than confirming it: it surfaced that flows.json still encodes the now-dead critique scope across three P0-adjacent flow names, that settled-decisions.md defines Art Loupe as including critique, and that no LLM dependency exists anywhere in the repo yet. Reading veloce-trace next door established what is actually portable instead of guessing. The proposal pushes back on Codex at the one place Codex's own evaluation flags a risk it does not then resolve — a fixed Director-to-Critic route is a workflow, not an agent system.
- **Improve:** ExitPlanMode was called without first saying plainly what approving would do. Laurie rejected it — 'I wasn't quite sure what I was approving' — and the repair was a single sentence that should have preceded the call: approving writes one gitignored markdown file and nothing else. Putting a 387-line deliverable document inside a plan file is exactly the case where 'approve the plan' reads as 'approve building this.' Separately, the first draft asserted that docs/temp-references was in-tree without running git check-ignore; it is gitignored, and the claim needed correcting after the fact. That is the same verify-late pattern the previous session's retro already flagged.
- **Tooling:** markdownlint walks docs/temp-references/ even though .gitignore excludes it, so pnpm check:all fails locally while CI stays green. A gate that disagrees with CI teaches people to ignore the gate. Either markdownlint should honour .gitignore or its ignore list should mirror it — the specific folder is disposable here, but the class of drift is not.
- **Decisions:**
  - Art Loupe is the final capstone pivot — the discharge app was left for personal defensibility, not because it was weaker
  - Scope is two feature-bearing apps (studio, operations); apps/entry stays as the built public shell and never grows a workflow
  - In-progress artwork critique is cut; its value folds into reference assessment at intake, a hand-applied self-check card, and the Plan Critic
  - The Plan Critic survives the cut and must be named as such — it critiques the plan, not the artwork
  - Proposed wedge: every plan claim is measured, cited, or chosen — the anti-confabulation spine, and the eval spine
  - Proposed that the graph must branch on tool results (complexity threshold, confidence interrupt, defect-driven re-retrieval), not only on intake answers
  - docs/temp-references is transient and gitignored; its markdownlint failures will not be fixed because the folder goes away with the design docs
  - Pending Laurie's answers: showcase vision tool, the Week 9 fine-tuning story, and whether voice is in scope

### 2026-08-30 — Repo reset prep, static-check repair, and a 92 kB client-bundle fix

- **Went well:** The static checks earned their cost within an hour of being wired up: they surfaced a WebKit e2e run where no CSS loaded at all, a dependency graph that had been rendering empty, a `circular` check that had never once executed, and a 92 kB gzipped Zod leak on the simplest page in the repo. Root causes came from measurement rather than guesswork — per-browser geometry, gzipped chunk inventories, and reading routes-manifest.json — which is what turned 'entry is over budget' into a one-module fix instead of a threshold bump. Reading the code path rather than running the generator also caught an unguarded readdirSync that would have thrown on a fresh clone.
- **Improve:** The Q-number strip was done with regexes first, which broke prose at six sites that then needed hand repair; the explicit per-site replacement list used later for the issue numbers landed clean on the first pass and should have been the approach from the start. The options offered for that same question missed what was actually wanted — four alternatives, none chosen — costing a round trip that a plainer question would not have. Three factual claims about the report generators were also drafted from a plausible model and only then verified.
- **Tooling:** `check:all` covers neither `circular`, `size`, `depcruise` nor `depcruise:graph`, which is exactly how two of them rotted unnoticed — one had never run, another rendered an empty page. A static check outside the gate is a check nobody runs. Fold the cheap ones in, or accept that they are advisory and say so where they are defined.
- **Decisions:**
  - docs/design renamed to docs/contrast-report — the folder holds only generated output, so it is named for the report it produces
  - Vale stays advisory and outside check:all; the package set is still under evaluation and the prose cleanup is unfinished
  - Third-party agent skills stay pinned in skills-lock.json and never vendored — committing them means redistributing them
  - Node pinned in .nvmrc (24); all five CI setup-node steps switched to node-version-file so there is one source of truth
  - Git history reset rather than carried forward — fresh init, old history bundled outside the repo
  - ui-shell-spec Q-numbers and predecessor issue numbers stripped repo-wide: the explanations stay, the dangling pointers go
  - DISABLE_HTTPS_UPGRADE belongs on the Playwright build, not the served process — next build bakes headers() into routes-manifest.json
  - LAUNCH_TARGETS split into an import-free module so a client component cannot pull env validation, and Zod, across the boundary
  - docs/backlog.md is the interim deferral home until the GitHub project board exists; GitHub becomes the source of truth after that
  - Optional CLI tools (tree, graphviz, gh) documented in the README rather than vendored as devDependencies
